oceanmysterieshub A massive whale shark accidentally struck an aquarium diver with its powerful tail, revealing just how dangerous it can be to work alongside one of the ocean's largest creatures. The incident occurred while a staff member was cleaning inside a large aquarium tank. As the enormous shark swam through the confined space, its tail swept into the diver, delivering an unexpected impact. Despite the frightening moment, the contact appeared completely unintentional. Whale sharks are gentle filter feeders, but their incredible size, weight, and momentum can make even the slightest movement dangerous to anyone nearby. Aquarium divers regularly work within inches of marine animals that dwarf them in size. Even without aggression, a single unexpected movement can create a serious hazard. The footage serves as a powerful reminder that the ocean's gentlest giants still possess immense physical strength, even inside controlled environments. Step 1: unplug the heater, light, filter Step 2: siphon the substrate/ground Step 3: drain approx. 1/3 of the water  Step 4: dechlorinate the fresh water and fill up the aquarium Step 5: wipe the rim, edges, outside of the tank Step 6: feed your betta and show them some love. After closing time at a Japanese aquarium, this little otter grabs the broom and helps clean up. His reward for a tidy pool is a single ice cube, and he could not be happier. 🦦🧹🧊 Clips shared from Toba Aquarium in Mie show otters helping keepers tidy toys after hours and getting ice cubes in return. Toba is famous for its otters and is the only aquarium in Japan that keeps sea otters. Aquarium keepers use ice and toys as enrichment, because otters have a natural urge to bang and handle objects and ice helps them cool down. Marine mammal experts say this kind of play keeps captive animals mentally healthy, an animal welfare practice Toba staff say they use deliberately.
